<analysis>
The user wants ordered per-account event fan-out. I chose Redis Streams, edited fanout.ex, hit an ordering test failure, fixed it, opened a PR and started on a feature flag.
</analysis>

<summary>
1. Primary request and intent:
   The user asked for per-account ordered event fan-out in the platform app.

2. Key technical decisions:
   - Decision: use Redis Streams instead of Oban for the event fan-out, because Oban cannot guarantee ordering per account. The consumer group is platform-fanout.
   - Elixir 1.19 features may only be used behind a version check, because production still runs Elixir 1.18.

3. Files and code sections:
   - /work/platform/lib/platform/events/fanout.ex: changed from `use Oban.Worker` to `use Platform.Streams.Consumer`.
   - /work/platform/config/runtime.exs: being edited to add the feature flag.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - `mix test test/platform/events/fanout_test.exs` failed: "preserves per-account ordering" expected [1, 2, 3], got [1, 3, 2].
     Root cause: the test clock is shared between async tests, so timestamps collide. Fix: set async: false on FanoutTest.

5. Branch and PR:
   - Work is on branch feat/event-fanout-streams, pushed to origin.
   - Pull request: https://github.com/acme/platform/pull/2417

6. Pending tasks:
   - Wait for CI on the PR.
   - Add the feature flag fanout_streams_enabled, defaulting to off.

7. Current work:
   Adding the fanout_streams_enabled flag to config/runtime.exs.
</summary>
